approval.cost: No partner program fee, listing fee, or revenue share is stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: Two different gates depending on the path. OAuth apps: creation is CLOSED. The docs banner states: 'The ability to create new OAuth applications with Segment is no longer available' and 'The Enable with OAuth feature is a legacy option, compatible only with Destinations developed on Segment's original developer center. If you're interested in this feature for new Destinations, please let Segment know at partner-support@segment.com.' Catalog integrations: human review is required before end users can use your integration. 'Before users can go hands on with your integration, a review by Segment engineers is required to ensure the integration meets security and usability standards.' The Public Beta Checklist describes the Segment Developer Center team testing the submitted app (data-delivery test suite with a provided API key, documentation review, catalog entry review) before Public Beta approval: 'To maintain the quality of the partner integrations catalog, the Segment Developer Center team will carefully test your App once you have submitted it for review.' Review is triggered twice: requesting Developer Portal access (Segment reviews the request; docs advise including 'a valid company website and email address' and detailed use-case answers 'to expedite the approval process'), and submitting a Source/Destination for Private/Public Beta launch. Pre-approval, your integration stays in a private 'building' state, testable only in your own workspace. No install/user caps are stated.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration anywhere in the docs read)

blockers.detail: You cannot create a new Segment OAuth app at all. Any guide that presents 'register an OAuth app with Segment' as a current flow is describing a legacy, closed program; the only documented route to ask is partner-support@segment.com.
blockers.howToClear: Build on the partner catalog model (or use first-party tokens for a customer's own automation) instead of planning around OAuth.
blockers.title: The headline blocker: OAuth app creation is closed

blockers.detail: Segment explicitly warns that workspace tokens 'are only suitable for first party, trusted applications, such as your personal local scripts and server side programs. Partners should not prompt Segment users for their username and password and save an access token as a way to delegate access.'
blockers.howToClear: Never build a delegated-access product on customer workspace tokens; that is what the (closed) OAuth program and the catalog model are for.
blockers.title: The documented anti-pattern: faking delegation with workspace tokens

blockers.detail: Legacy OAuth: 'You set these scopes during app creation and when you start the install flow. You must use the same scope in both places, otherwise you get an invalid scope error.' If you need broader access you must 'create a new app with workspace permission and then re-install it'. Also: 'Developer Center Destinations must use their specific destination scope for their enable flows. More permissive apps are subject to revocation unless specifically approved.'
blockers.howToClear: For grandfathered apps, choose the narrowest scope (destination/<slug>) at creation; there is no upgrade path.
blockers.title: Scope is baked in at app creation (legacy OAuth)

alternatives: First-party Public API tokens (long-lived tokens created by a Workspace Owner under Settings > Workspace settings > Access Management > Tokens, sent as Authorization: Bearer; for a customer's OWN automation, explicitly 'only suitable for first party, trusted applications'. The older Config API also uses workspace access tokens, but 'As of February 1, 2024, new Config API tokens cannot be created in the app'; contact Segment support)

Legacy Enable with OAuth (documented but CLOSED to new apps): an 'App' in the Developer Center that 'behaves like a standard OAuth client, but adds granular permissions'; a Workspace Owner authorizes it on a specific workspace and source, Segment creates an App Install, and 'the token returned by Segment isn't tied to a user, it's tied to an App Install'
flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists for new apps. The real third-party path is a partner-built catalog integration (Source or Destination) in the Segment Developer Center
flavor.why: Segment's OAuth feature is called 'Enable with OAuth' (a.k.a. 'Enable with Segment'), and the object is an 'App' created in the Segment Developer Center. But the docs now carry this banner verbatim: 'The ability to create new OAuth applications with Segment is no longer available.' What actually exists today: you join the Segment Select Partner Program, get Developer Center/Portal access, and build a Source or Destination (new destinations are built on the Actions framework). Segment customers then 'connect' your product from inside their own workspace via the Segment catalog: for a destination, the customer picks your destination on a source and enters YOUR product's credentials (typically an API key for your service) into Segment; for a cloud source, the customer pastes the Segment write key into your product's settings. Segment does not run an OAuth consent flow into your product for standard catalog integrations.

humanMust: Sign up for the Segment Select Partner Program and agree to the Segment Partner Program Agreement
Request Developer Center/Developer Portal access (Segment account, company website, email, integration use-case details)
Add catalog metadata and write the integration's documentation (Segment's docs team works with you)
Submit the integration for review (destinations via the 'Submit a pull request' flow; sources via 'Submit for review' in the Developer Portal)
name: Segment
nuances: Legacy OAuth figures (the only place Segment states token lifetimes): install/access tokens live 1 hour ('Tokens expire every hour, so your token might have expired'; token responses show expires_in 3599/3600). There is NO OAuth refresh-token grant: you re-mint by calling the installation token API with your client credentials (GET platform.segmentapis.com/v1beta/$INSTALL_NAME/token with HTTP Basic auth), 'The token expires in an hour, so do this periodically'.

Legacy OAuth mechanics: 'Segment only accepts response_type=code'; the authorize URL is id.segmentapis.com/oauth2/auth, the token endpoint is id.segmentapis.com/oauth2/token (code + redirect_uri, client ID/secret in a Basic header), and Config API calls use the install token as Bearer. 'The user must also be a Workspace Owner of the authorized workspace', and as a destination partner 'you may only manage your own destination on the workspace and source authorized by the user'. Re-running the flow on an installed workspace returns an 'install already exists' error; store the install_name and reuse it.

Legacy OAuth rigidities: 'You can have five redirect_uris on app creation. Editing the app info directly is not supported. Contact Segment if you want any of your redirect_uris or other info changed.' Segment does echo back the state parameter if you set one, and the redirect_uri must be sent again in the token request.

Catalog and token gating: the Public API 'is available for Team and Business tier customers', and only Workspace Owners can create Public API tokens. When building a direct destination, 'once created you will not be able to change the destination slug'.
prerequisites: A Segment Select Partner Program signup (Partner Program Agreement)
A Segment account for Developer Portal access and sandbox testing
For the customer side: a workspace where your integration can be selected from the catalog

steps.detail: Sign up for the Segment Select Partner Program and agree to the Segment Partner Program Agreement. Then request Developer Center/Portal access with a Segment account, company website, email, and detailed integration use-case answers (docs advise detail 'to expedite the approval process').
steps.title: Join the Select Partner Program; request Developer Portal access

steps.detail: In the Developer Portal, create the integration (name and slug; destinations are built on the Actions framework). Your own Segment account doubles as a sandbox to test in a private 'building' state. Note: 'once created you will not be able to change the destination slug'.
steps.title: Build your Source or Destination

steps.detail: Add catalog metadata and write your integration's documentation; Segment's docs team works with you on the docs.
steps.title: Add catalog metadata and documentation

steps.detail: Submit for review (destinations via the 'Submit a pull request' flow; sources via 'Submit for review'). The Developer Center team tests the app (data-delivery test suite, documentation review, catalog entry review). Launch proceeds Private Beta, then Public Beta / Public in the catalog.
steps.title: Submit for review; launch to beta, then public

steps.detail: The customer finds your integration in the catalog inside their workspace, selects a source, and enters the credentials for your product (e.g. your API key). There is no OAuth redirect for your app to automate in this model.
steps.title: Customer connects from the catalog

steps.detail: Create an App in the Developer Center (App Info > OAuth for the Client ID and Client Secret), register up to five redirect URLs, and set the scope (destination/<slug> recommended, workspace:read, or workspace). Redirect the authorizing Workspace Owner to id.segmentapis.com/oauth2/auth?response_type=code&scope=...&client_id=...; exchange the code at id.segmentapis.com/oauth2/token for an Install Token; call the Config API with it as Bearer; re-mint hourly via the installation token API with Basic auth.
steps.title: Legacy reference: Enable with OAuth (closed to new apps)

tagline: Segment's third-party OAuth program is closed to new apps. The documented routes today are partner-built catalog integrations (gated by Segment's partner program and an engineer review) or first-party workspace API tokens, which Segment explicitly says partners must not use to fake delegated access.
